tickets.title: [Spec] Claude team takeover and self-improving workflow
tickets.body:
# Claude team takeover and self-improving workflow

## Problem Statement

The remaining marketplace work is spread across one integration branch, nineteen Codex worktrees, four Codex threads that stopped on a usage limit, and a planning directory whose receipts describe what Codex did but not what a successor should do next. The "retrospective after every ticket, apply every learning" rule exists only as prose; nothing refuses an integration or a publication when a unit has no retro record or leaves a finding open, so the rule depends on each agent remembering it. Learnings from earlier units landed in long narrative documents that every agent loads whole, rather than in the directory that needs them. Ticket state has to be reconstructed from GitHub, the plan narrative and private evidence packets each time. When the maintainer wants to know what another agent did, the only route is reading multi-hundred-megabyte transcripts by hand.

## Solution

Make the Claude Code session the integration owner under the same contract Codex followed, and turn the workflow rules into things the repository enforces. One deterministic retro gate runs the same way from a mise task, from git hooks and from Claude Code hooks, so a unit cannot be integrated or published without a complete retro record. Learnings have a fixed destination by kind: mechanical rules become checks, judgement rules go to a reviewer-only standards file, navigation goes to the nearest directory guidance file, repeated workflows become skills, roles become project agents. Ticket and lane state are generated into a ledger from the tracker and the lane records instead of being retyped. A `codex-session-history` skill turns Codex's native records into bounded digests so a successor can resume another agent's work from evidence. Codex keeps a compatible role and configuration surface so it can rejoin after its limit resets.

## User Stories

1. As the maintainer, I want a dated activation record of the takeover with exact checkout, HEAD, remote and granted authority, so that no agent has to guess who may write.
2. As the maintainer, I want every Codex worktree, branch and private evidence packet treated as a read-only import source, so that uncommitted Codex work is never lost or overwritten.
3. As an implementer agent, I want one lane record per unit naming my worktree, branch, base commit, path allowlist, reviewer and required checks, so that I can start without reconstructing ownership.
4. As the merger, I want to refuse a lane whose changed paths leave its allowlist, so that two lanes cannot silently edit the same file.
5. As the maintainer, I want integration and publication to fail closed when a unit's retro record is missing or has an open finding without an owner, so that the retro rule holds for humans, Claude and Codex alike.
6. As a human developer, I want the retro gate runnable as one mise task from any shell, so that I can check a unit the same way the agents do.
7. As the maintainer, I want the gate to run as a git `pre-merge-commit` and `pre-push` step through `hk`, so that enforcement survives a different agent or no agent at all.
8. As the maintainer, I want Claude Code to deny `git merge`, `git push` and the publication task when the gate fails, and to hold an implementer's stop until its retro draft exists, so that the harness enforces the rule before git does.
9. As a retro writer, I want a fixed record shape (seven categories, severity-ordered findings, a disposition and verification per finding), so that a gate can check it mechanically and a reviewer can read it quickly.
10. As the maintainer, I want each actionable retro finding routed to one destination by kind, so that the next agent meets the learning where it works instead of in a growing narrative.
11. As any agent, I want the root guidance file to stay a short navigation pointer and each directory to carry its own guidance that loads only when I touch that directory, so that context is spent where it matters.
12. As a reviewer agent, I want judgement-only standards in a reviewer-facing file, so that implementers are not loaded with rules they cannot check mechanically.
13. As the maintainer, I want project agent definitions for implementer, documentation writer, reviewer, retro writer and extractor with their model and effort, so that lane dispatch is a reference, not a prompt rewrite.
14. As the maintainer, I want the ticket ledger regenerated from the live tracker graph and the lane records, so that frontier, blockers and lane state are never hand-edited.
15. As the maintainer, I want the workflow vocabulary (unit, lane, gate, frontier, merger, integration tip, retro barrier, receipt, admission) defined in the glossary, so that specs, tickets and records use one language.
16. As a future reader, I want an architecture decision record for the takeover and the mechanical gate, so that the trade-off is explained where someone will look for it.
17. As a successor agent, I want to resolve a Codex thread link to its rollout, judge whether it is live, digest it boundedly, list its research receipts and cite ordinals, so that I can take over without reading raw transcripts.
18. As the maintainer, I want the skill's scripts hermetically tested against synthetic records and kept byte-identical in the two skill directories, so that both agent families load the same thing.
19. As a Codex user returning after the limit resets, I want Codex's project roles and configuration to describe the same lanes and gate, so that Codex can pick up a lane under the same rules.
20. As the maintainer, I want the `.gitignore` additions the lanes need handled as a reviewed baseline transition that keeps the original nineteen hashes as historical evidence, so that the frozen acceptance inputs are not changed silently.
21. As the maintainer, I want candidate plugins, skills, mods and tools evaluated with evidence before adoption, so that the toolset grows by decision rather than by accumulation.
22. As the maintainer, I want host-heavy lanes to run one at a time behind an explicit per-run confirmation, so that compiler builds never collide with the single capacity lease.
23. As the maintainer, I want every unit's state (planned, implemented, tested, reviewed, retro, committed, integrated, published, closed) recorded separately, so that a static pass is never mistaken for acceptance.
24. As the maintainer, I want publication to keep using the existing scanned delivery route, so that a leak cannot leave the machine through a Claude lane.

## Implementation Decisions

- Ownership: the Claude session is the sole integration writer and canonical plan owner; implementers write only inside their lane's allowlist; a separate merger integrates serially; reviewers own no files. Lanes live under the repository's Claude worktree directory on `claude/<unit>-<slug>` branches cut from the integration tip; the lane record is JSON so a gate can read it.
- Retro gate: one script checks that the record exists for the unit derived from the branch name or an explicit argument, that all seven categories are addressed, that at least one verification binding (exit code, hash or named check) is present, and that no finding is open without an owner or blocker. It exposes the result as a mise task; `hk` runs that task on `pre-merge-commit` and `pre-push`; Claude Code settings hooks deny `git merge`, `git push` and the publication task on failure and block an implementer's stop once when its retro draft is missing. The gate judges shape and bindings only; judgement stays with the reviewer.
- Learning destinations: mechanical → a deterministic check in the existing check runner or a mise task; judgement → the reviewer-only standards file; navigation → the nearest directory guidance file or a path-scoped rule; repeated workflow → a skill; role → a project agent; harness behaviour → a hook. The retro writer applies in-scope findings itself and hands cross-scope edits to the parent.
- Guidance hierarchy: the root guidance file stays a pointer; each top-level working directory gets its own guidance file plus a thin importer so both agent families read the same text; path-scoped rules load lazily on file access.
- Ledger: a generator reads the tracker's parent and blocking relationships and the lane records, and writes the ledger table; hand-maintained columns are limited to local evidence notes.
- Codex compatibility: the project's Codex role definitions and configuration are updated to name the same roles, lanes and gate; the existing cross-agent skill directory mirrors the Claude skill directory byte for byte, enforced by a test.
- Baseline: the frozen nineteen acceptance inputs are changed only through a versioned, reviewed baseline transition that retains the original hashes as historical evidence; local-only ignores use the repository's local exclude file until then.
- Models: Opus for code lanes, Sonnet for documentation lanes, Fable for review, retro and synthesis, Haiku for mechanical extraction; up to four offline lanes concurrently, one host-heavy lane with per-run confirmation.
- Publication and closure: the existing scanned delivery route publishes the integration branch; tickets close one at a time through the qualified closure operation with bound acceptance evidence.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test exercises an external seam and asserts observable behaviour: a CLI exit code and output, a file the user reads, a hook's JSON decision, a tracker read-back. Tests that mirror implementation structure are not written.
- Seam 1 — gate CLI: fixture retro records (complete, missing category, open finding, no evidence) drive the gate's exit codes and reason lines; discovered by the existing check runner like every development test.
- Seam 2 — hook contract: the hook scripts are fed Claude Code's stdin JSON shapes (`PreToolUse` with a Bash command, `SubagentStop`, `Stop` with `stop_hook_active`) and must emit the exact deny/block/allow shapes; `hk`'s steps are exercised in a scratch repository.
- Seam 3 — skill scripts: a synthetic rollout, synthetic receipts and a minimal thread index under a temporary `CODEX_HOME`; the real record stores are never read in tests.
- Seam 4 — existing named checks: task validation, the static check, the nineteen-hash baseline and diff whitespace run on every lane and on the composed tree at integration; static passes are recorded as static, never as runtime, provider, fresh-session or container acceptance.
- Prior art: the development tests for tracker creation, edges, delivery and research refresh, which already use fake clients, durable journals and scratch repositories.

## Out of Scope

Implementing or closing the existing spec #11 and #83 tickets (they proceed under their own graphs; the Phase C closures are carried by T3 #93 and T4 #101); the agent-protocol / dynamic-agents package and its skills outside this repository; changing the four-hour research heartbeat; new paid provider research; host-heavy compiler work; merging to `main`; global Claude or Codex settings, hooks, trust or credentials; moving skills into dotfiles.

## Further Notes

Decisions were settled in two grilling rounds on 2026-10-13 with every recommendation accepted; the activation record and the plan's takeover section carry the exact state. Stage invocation modes are recorded in the plan's skill-invocations record: the user pasted `/grill-with-docs` as text in the first prompt (the harness did not expand it; the router body ran file-guided) and its `grilling` and `domain-modeling` skills ran natively; `to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `implement-spec` and `retro` were applied as file-guided fallbacks from the installed skill files under the user's standing authorization, the same mode Codex recorded, and run natively only when the user types them. Research for this spec reuses existing receipts: the hook and rules reference was verified against current Claude Code documentation (v2.1.296) and the Codex record stores were inspected directly; no provider research was run because Context7 is quota-blocked and Firecrawl returns HTTP 402. Lanes from this spec are recorded in `lanes/*.json` and their tickets in `ticket-ledger.md`; `implement-spec` runs them as the wave plan in `task_plan.md` under the ticket-frontier skill. The end-of-spec `code-review` starts from `start_sha` `361688e` (D10), the tip the first CT lane was cut from. A UI mod for the grilling questions is ticket CT-13 (D14).
